office_does: The county auditor runs Stevens County's elections and voter registration, records deeds and documents, licenses vehicles and vessels, and keeps the county's financial accounts.
race_blurb: Two-term Auditor Lori Larsen faces Eric Simpson, a logger who chairs the county Republican Party's election integrity committee; both prefer the Republican Party. Simpson calls vote-by-mail a catastrophe and wants hand counts and voter-list cleaning; Larsen defends the current system and runs on her record. Larsen led the primary 58% to 40%.

candidates.summary: Stevens County Auditor since 2018, with a doctorate in public policy, running on her record of election administration, records access and licensing changes.
highlights: Auditor since 2018; won 61.6% in 2018 and was unopposed in 2022 [S11][S12]
Co-wrote a 2025 column defending Washington's vote-at-home system as secure and cost-effective [S6]
Says she administers election law as written and would implement any change the Legislature or Congress makes [S5]
Cites clean financial reports, online records access, deed-fraud alerts and licensing changes [S1][S4][S5]

experience.basis: Eight-year incumbent running on her record, qualifications and statewide auditor roles.

reform.basis: Defends the existing vote-at-home system and frames her role as administering current law, not changing it.

spending.basis: Says she keeps costs low with a conservative approach to taxpayer resources, though she also sought grant-funded new equipment.

candidates.summary: Logger, welder and precinct committee officer who chairs the county Republican Party's election integrity committee, running to change how Stevens County runs elections.
highlights: Calls vote-by-mail a 'catastrophe' and proposes hand counting ballots and proactive cleaning of the voter list [S2][S4]
Says he lacks professional background in the auditor's duties but would complete all training [S2][S4]
Promises 'responsible stewardship of your money' and alleges poor financial stewardship in the office [S1][S2]
Raised $38,740 to Larsen's $6,900 through early October [S7]

experience.basis: First-time candidate for the office who says he does not have Larsen's experience and runs as a change from the current system.

reform.basis: Campaign centers on overhauling election administration: hand counts, voter-list purges and opposition to vote-by-mail.

spending.basis: Promises responsible stewardship and alleges poor financial stewardship in the office, without a specific audit program.
